title: Moderation
description: Keep your community safe with a complete toolkit for warnings, mutes, bans, channel control and member management. Every action respects role hierarchy and is written to your mod log as a numbered case.

commands.name: warn
commands.summary: Issue a formal warning to a member.
commands.description: Records a warning against a member, notifies them by direct message and logs it as a case. Warnings build a member's record, so you can review it later with `/warnings` or `/history`.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to warn. They must be in the server.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why the member is being warned (up to 512 characters).

examples.note: Aria receives a DM and the warning is saved as a case.

notes: The reply tells you the case number and how many active warnings the member now has.
You can only warn members whose highest role is below yours and below Damselette's.

commands.name: warnings
commands.description: Lists the active warnings for a member, newest last, including the date, the moderator who issued each one and the reason. Warnings that were removed with `/delwarn` or `/clearwarnings` are not shown here; use `/history` to see everything.

options.name: user
options.description: The member whose warnings you want to see.

notes: Only you can see the reply.
The most recent 15 warnings are displayed.

commands.name: delwarn
commands.summary: Remove a single warning by its case number.
commands.description: Marks one warning as removed. The case stays in the member's `/history` (flagged as removed) so there is always an audit trail, but it no longer counts as an active warning.

options.name: case
options.description: The case number of the warning, shown when it was issued and in the mod log.

notes: Only warnings can be removed this way. Other case types, such as bans, are permanent records.

commands.name: clearwarnings
commands.summary: Remove every active warning from a member.
commands.description: Clears all of a member's active warnings in one go, for example after a probation period. The cleared cases remain visible in `/history` as removed.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to clear.

notes: The reply confirms how many warnings were cleared.

commands.name: history
commands.summary: View a user's complete moderation history.
commands.description: Shows every moderation case recorded for a user in this server: warnings, mutes, kicks, bans and more. Removed warnings are included and marked, making this the definitive record when reviewing a member.

options.name: user
options.description: The user to look up. They do not need to still be in the server.

notes: Only you can see the reply.
The 15 most recent cases are displayed, with the total count in the title.

commands.name: mute
commands.summary: Temporarily mute a member using Discord's timeout.
commands.description: Places a member in timeout for a set time, so they cannot send messages, react, speak in voice or join video until it ends. The member is notified by direct message and the case is logged with its duration.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to mute.

options.name: duration
options.description: How long the mute lasts, such as `10m`, `2h`, `1d` or `1h30m`. Maximum 28 days.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason for the mute (up to 512 characters).

notes: Accepted units: `s` seconds, `m` minutes, `h` hours, `d` days and `w` weeks.
Discord does not allow muting server administrators or the server owner.

commands.name: unmute
commands.description: Removes an active mute so the member can talk again straight away. The action is logged as a case.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to release.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason for lifting the mute (up to 512 characters).

notes: Fails with a friendly message if the member is not currently muted.

commands.name: kick
commands.summary: Remove a member from the server (they can rejoin).
commands.description: Removes a member from the server. They can return with a fresh invite. The member is notified by direct message before the kick and the case is logged.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to kick. They must be in the server.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason for the kick (up to 512 characters).

commands.name: ban
commands.summary: Permanently ban a user, optionally deleting their recent messages.
commands.description: Bans a user from the server. The user is notified by direct message, the ban is applied and the case is logged. You can also wipe up to seven days of their message history in the same step.

options.name: user
options.description: The user to ban. They do not need to be in the server.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason for the ban (up to 512 characters).

options.name: delete_days
options.description: Days of the user's messages to delete, from 0 to 7. Defaults to 0.

examples.note: Bans the user and removes the last day of their messages.

notes: Hierarchy checks apply to members who are still in the server.

commands.name: softban
commands.summary: Ban and instantly unban to clear a user's recent messages.
commands.description: Bans a member and immediately unbans them, which deletes the last seven days of their messages while allowing them to rejoin. It is ideal for cleaning up after compromised accounts or message spam without a permanent ban.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to softban. They must be in the server.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason (up to 512 characters).

notes: The direct message tells the member they are free to rejoin.

commands.name: unban
commands.summary: Lift a ban using the user's ID.
commands.description: Removes a ban so the user can rejoin with a new invite. Because banned users are no longer in your member list, you identify them by their Discord user ID.

options.name: user_id
options.description: The numeric Discord ID of the banned user.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason for the unban (up to 512 characters).

notes: To copy a user ID, enable Developer Mode in Discord's advanced settings, then right-click the user.

commands.name: purge
commands.summary: Bulk delete recent messages in the current channel.
commands.description: Deletes up to 100 recent messages in the channel where you run it, optionally only those sent by one user. The action is logged as a case so there is a record of who cleaned the channel.

options.name: amount
options.description: How many messages to delete, from 1 to 100.

options.name: user
options.description: Only delete messages sent by this user.

examples.note: Removes up to 20 of that user's messages from the latest 100 in the channel.

notes: Discord only allows bulk deletion of messages newer than 14 days; older messages are skipped.
When filtering by user, Damselette looks through the 100 most recent messages in the channel.
The confirmation is only visible to you.

commands.name: slowmode
commands.summary: Set or remove a channel's slowmode delay.
commands.description: Sets how long members must wait between messages in a text channel. Use it to calm busy channels during raids or heated discussions, and set it to `0` to switch it off.

options.name: seconds
options.description: Delay between messages in seconds, from 0 (off) to 21600 (6 hours).

options.name: channel
options.description: A text channel. Defaults to the channel you run the command in.

examples.note: Ten seconds between messages in this channel.

commands.name: lock
commands.summary: Stop everyone from sending messages in a channel.
commands.description: Prevents the `@everyone` role from sending messages in a text channel, which is useful for emergencies and announcements. Roles that have been explicitly granted permission to speak, such as moderators, are not affected. The lock is logged as a case.

options.name: channel
options.description: A text channel. Defaults to the current channel.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason recorded in the case log (up to 512 characters).

notes: Reverse it with `/unlock`.

commands.name: unlock
commands.summary: Let everyone send messages in a channel again.
commands.description: Removes the lock placed by `/lock` by resetting the `@everyone` send-messages permission, so the channel goes back to following its category and server defaults. The action is logged as a case.

options.name: channel
options.description: A text channel. Defaults to the current channel.

commands.name: nickname
commands.summary: Change or reset a member's nickname.
commands.description: Sets a new server nickname for a member, or resets it back to their username when you leave the nickname empty. You can always change your own nickname with it, provided Damselette can manage it.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to rename.

options.name: nickname
options.description: The new nickname, up to 32 characters. Leave empty to reset.

notes: Hierarchy rules apply when you change someone else's nickname.

commands.name: role
commands.summary: Add or remove a role from a member.
commands.description: Assigns or removes a role without opening Discord's member panel. Damselette checks that both you and the bot sit above the role, so it can never be used to hand out roles higher than your own.

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.summary: Give a role to a member.

options.name: user
options.description: The member who will receive the role.

options.name: role
options.description: The role to give.

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.summary: Take a role away from a member.

options.name: user
options.description: The member who will lose the role.

options.name: role
options.description: The role to remove.

notes: The role must be below your highest role (the server owner is exempt) and below Damselette's highest role.
Integration-managed roles and `@everyone` cannot be assigned manually.

commands.name: voicekick
commands.summary: Disconnect a member from their voice channel.
commands.description: Removes a member from the voice channel they are currently in without removing them from the server. The action is logged as a case.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to disconnect.

options.name: reason
options.description: Reason for the disconnect (up to 512 characters).

notes: The member must currently be connected to a voice channel.
